title: proofmass-check results
description: What one run of proofmass-check found. Lengths in m, angles in rad, masses in kg, times in s.

spec_version.description: The version of docs/spec.md the checks follow.

sha256.description: Of the root USD file only, not of the layers it references.

name.description: As on the command line, for example physx or newton.

floor.description: The floor height, or null for a run without a floor.

engine_cannot_run.description: Checks that apply to the asset but that the engine cannot run yet: they are N/A, and a PASS does not cover them (docs/spec.md, section 5). Older results do not have it.

gripper_without_site.description: Joints that look like a gripper's fingers on an asset with no gripper site: GRIP and SHAKE did not run on it (docs/spec.md, section 3). Older results do not have it.

wheels_without_mobile.description: Joints that look like wheels on an asset whose root layer has no SimReady_Metadata.mobile: the wheeled checks did not run on it (docs/spec.md, section 3). Older results do not have it.

detail.description: The measured numbers, or why the check does not apply.

measurements.description: Each number the check compared with its rule (docs/spec.md, section 6). A check that did not apply has none.

subject.description: A joint, a gripper site, or empty for the whole asset.

case.description: Which test of the subject, for example 25% or upper. Can be empty.

value.description: null when the engine gave a value that is not finite.

limit.description: The rule's limit. null for a number the check reports but does not judge.

bound.description: max: the rule wants value <= limit. min: value >= limit.

ok.description: What the check decided for this number.

passed.description: True when no check failed and the run did not stop with an error.

error.description: Present when the run stopped with an error.

replay.description: Present for a run with --replay: the file, next to this one, with the motion of every body in each check (docs/gui.md, section 5.5). Its header carries the same id, which is new for each run.

file.description: A file name, without a folder.
